control_need.evidence: I was nervous about the competition and then I became my own competition raising the bar every year, pushing, pushing, pushing myself as hard as I knew.

uncertainty_tolerance.evidence: You don’t have to know all the right moves—you just need to know the next one.

trust_propensity.evidence: So, I don’t have a lot of friends. Everybody knows Gayle. There’s Gayle, there’s Maria, there’s Bob. And that’s—that’s about it, you know?

risk_appetite.evidence: A few years ago I decided, as you will at some point, that it was time to recalculate, find new territory, break new ground.

self_efficacy.evidence: At no time did I ever feel out of place, or not enough, or inadequate—or an impostor. Because I knew who I was.

autonomy_need.evidence: Being myself was much easier than pretending to be Barbara Walters. I figured out, oh gee, I can be a much better Oprah than I could be a pretend Barbara.

intimacy_need.evidence: What we want, the common denominator that I found in every single interview, is we want to be validated. We want to be understood.

status_sensitivity.evidence: I was stressed and I was frustrated and quite frankly I was actually I was embarrassed.

empathy_reactivity.evidence: People always ask the wrong question when dealing with children with behavioral issues. They ask, “what’s wrong with you”, instead of, “what happened to you.”

core_models.name: 内在导航（still small voice）
core_models.rule: 遇到抉择时不外求答案，而是向内倾听'下一步正确动作'，把不确定拆成可执行的当下一步。
evidence: The key to life is to develop an internal moral, emotional G.P.S. that can tell you which way to go.
Every right move I’ve made has come from listening deeply and following that still, small voice.

core_models.name: 失败即重定向
core_models.rule: 所有挫折都被解释为'生命把你推向另一方向'，而非终点，从而保持行动而非停滞。
evidence: There is no such thing as failure.
Failure is just life trying to move us in another direction.

core_models.name: 共情验证是人类通用分母
core_models.rule: 任何互动的底层需求都是'被看见/被听见/这样可以吗'，因此沟通首要任务是给予验证。
evidence: Friends and family, yours, enemies, strangers in every argument in every encounter, every exchange I will tell you, they all want to know one thing: was that okay?
Did you hear me? Do you see me? Did what I say mean anything to you?

core_models.name: 创伤重构（what happened to you）
core_models.rule: 把行为问题重新框定为经历问题，承认过去并将其转为力量资源，而非归咎于人。
evidence: They ask, “what’s wrong with you”, instead of, “what happened to you.”
Everything that happened to you can also be a strength builder if you allow it.

core_models.name: 存在＞头衔（who you want to be）
core_models.rule: 评估自身与他人时看'你想成为谁'和'为什么'，而非成就/金钱/名气清单。
evidence: It’s a résumé that doesn’t just tell a story about what you want to accomplish but why.
Do not equate money and fame with accomplishment and character.

core_models.name: 接纳当下反抗即痛苦
core_models.rule: 对无法改变的现实先接纳'它就是这样'，抵抗只会放大痛苦，然后再选择行动。
evidence: Accept this moment for what it is.
Tell yourself, this is what it is—holding on causes more pain than accepting that.

heuristics.then: 允许自己短暂哀悼，然后宣告'这会过去、我会转好并变得更强'
heuristics.evidence: Trouble don’t last always. This too shall pass. I am going to turn this thing around and I will be better for it.

heuristics.then: 只找下一步正确动作，不强求一次看清全部
heuristics.evidence: You don’t have to know all the right moves—you just need to know the next one.

heuristics.if: 被要求扮演别人或某种模板
heuristics.then: 回到做自己，因为做真实的自己比模仿更省力更好
heuristics.evidence: I figured out, oh gee, I can be a much better Oprah than I could be a pretend Barbara.

heuristics.if: 面对愤世嫉俗或焦虑氛围
heuristics.then: 把它定义为敌人并选择希望、行动去对抗
heuristics.evidence: You have to declare war on one of our most dangerous enemies. That is cynicism.

heuristics.if: 看到社会问题过于庞大
heuristics.then: 挑一个具体问题、对至少一个人做一件好事就开始
heuristics.evidence: Pick a problem, any problem and do something about it.

heuristics.if: 在对抗性采访中收到敏感回答
heuristics.then: 复述并确认对方原话，用'我听到你说'固定事实边界
heuristics.evidence: I hear that you’re saying it was not your grandmother or grandfather.

heuristics.then: 先用自嘲式身体化幽默缓解，再回到主旨
heuristics.evidence: It was either that or a bag of Oreos. So I chose the shower.

heuristics.then: 把归因从个人道德转向结构/生物机制，释放羞耻
heuristics.evidence: to hear all along it’s you fighting your brain.

internal_conflicts.force_a: 反对羞耻与减肥文化的道德立场（'let’s stop the shaming and blaming'）
internal_conflicts.force_b: 长期作为减肥文化商业受益者与WeightWatchers/药企品牌绑定
internal_conflicts.behavioral_signature: 口头忏悔'I have been a major contributor'的同时仍在WW品牌与药企合作方框架下办节目，随后才退董事会、捐股——先说A、后补救B（dim05 #4/#6/#11）

internal_conflicts.force_a: 宣称'do not equate money and fame with accomplishment'的价值观
internal_conflicts.force_b: 实际反复以股权、董事席位、播客独家分销等资本化动作扩张影响力
internal_conflicts.behavioral_signature: 演讲贬低金钱名气，决策链却是买股入董事会、分批出售OWN股权、与Amazon签独家（dim05 #2/#3/#4/#10）

internal_conflicts.force_a: 对掌控与'自己做主'的强烈需求（became my own competition）
internal_conflicts.force_b: 现实需要资本方接管以维持网络生存
internal_conflicts.behavioral_signature: 把OWN多数股权逐步卖给Discovery至约95%，保留'才艺/品牌'角色却让出控制权（dim05 #2/#3）

internal_conflicts.force_a: 'be the truth'、无感知利益冲突的自我期许
internal_conflicts.force_b: 被外界反复读作'infomercial'与利益冲突
internal_conflicts.behavioral_signature: 先解释'I wanted no perceived conflict of interest'、退董事会，但节目仍以WW CEO与药物策略为核心嘉宾（dim05 #12）

emotion_triggers.trigger: 公开被媒体宣判失败（USA Today头条）
emotion_triggers.reaction: 压力、挫败、尴尬，躲进淋浴长时间独处
emotion_triggers.escalation: 把痛苦转成宣言式反弹——'I am going to turn this thing around and I will be better for it.'

emotion_triggers.trigger: 长期被当成'国民笑料'的体重羞辱
emotion_triggers.reaction: 承接并内化羞耻，反复自责'I’m smart enough to figure this out'
emotion_triggers.escalation: 把个人羞耻升级为公共运动，呼吁'stop the shaming and blaming'、'There’s no place for it.'

emotion_triggers.trigger: 对抗性采访中被追问敏感事实（种族、王室）
emotion_triggers.reaction: 降速、复述确认'I just wanted to make sure that I had the conversation correctly'
emotion_triggers.escalation: 把追问正当化为公众知情权——'I’m asking this because the public is going to want to know.'

emotion_triggers.trigger: 被指节目像减肥药软广告
emotion_triggers.reaction: 先承认自己是减肥文化'major contributor'与'biggest regrets'
emotion_triggers.escalation: 以'I’m no longer on the board, y’all, so I can ask that question'与'what’s the point of WeightWatchers now?'重新夺回提问权

blind_spots: 把结构性/政治性肥胖议题收敛为个人自由与胜利叙事，窄化了解决方案框架 [纽约时报 Tressie McMillan Cottom-2024]
身体正向批评者认为节目实为隐性软广并强化'缩小身体＝幸福'的框架 [The Cut-2024]
在WeightWatchers品牌下'拆解减肥文化'的自相矛盾未被自身察觉 [The Cut WW跟进-2024]
以个人信任与情感共鸣代替证据审查，早期为Dr. Oz平台化提供可信度 [BMJ研究者-2014 / John Oliver Last Week Tonight-2014]
把情感权威与医学证据、商业背书的边界模糊化，医生与药企顾问关系加剧质疑 [The Hollywood Reporter-2024]
以个人信任为核心搭建的项目在治理/保护机制上存在盲点 [NPR 领导力学院丑闻-2007]

causal_rules.description: 高自我效能叠加高自主需求时，倾向于拒绝模板、坚持'做自己'并把身份作为不可动摇的锚点
causal_rules.disposition: 以真实自我为决策基准，抗拒外部认同侵蚀（'because I knew who I was'）
causal_rules.behavioral_notes: 在压力情境中先稳住自我叙事再行动；但也使其难以先认领批评者指出的结构性盲点

causal_rules.description: 高控制需求遇到公开失败时，会先短暂退缩独处，随后转为宣言式重掌控制
causal_rules.disposition: 把失败迅速重构为'重定向'并对外宣布翻盘
causal_rules.behavioral_notes: OWN失败后从淋浴独处到Harvard宣告'I have turned that network around'；情绪修复走'哀悼→宣言'两拍

causal_rules.description: 高共情反应性使其在冲突/追问中优先给予验证与复述，而非正面对抗
causal_rules.disposition: 用'I hear you / was that okay'式验证降温，把对立转成理解
causal_rules.behavioral_notes: Harry/Meghan采访中反复确认对方原话；风险是共情权威被误读为证据审查（见盲点）

causal_rules.description: 较低信任倾向使其人际圈极窄但把公众关系高度制度化
causal_rules.disposition: 亲密圈仅少数几人，却对陌生大众持开放共情
causal_rules.behavioral_notes: 'I don’t have a lot of friends…Gayle, Maria, Bob'与'35,000 interviews'共存；亲密少、触达广
